Nah, you only update the bios when something doesn't work that's bios related. Updates to bios aren't going to affect performance at all, and, while easy enough, the consequences for screwing up often mean a bricked component, and it is easier to screw them up than say, a driver update. Additionally, even if you install everything right, they have the potential to break your system, because the motherboard manufacturer doesn't have your exact hardware configuration to test with. Don't update your damn BIOS unless you are having issues getting all of your ram working, and you have confirmed that both your sticks and all of your slots work, or something like that.
